page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is a virtual workstation instance from the compute-optimized with GPU family. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 23 GB of system RAM. Hardware acceleration is provided by a fractional 0.25 slice of an NVIDIA T4 GPU with 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include local NVMe or SSD storage and relies on network volumes, connected via a 2 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark outcomes place the compute performance in the lower tiers compared to modern cloud instances. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores reach 904.0 and 2011.0 respectively, while the PassMark CPU score is 3597.24, reflecting the aging Intel Skylake-generation architecture. Uncached memory bandwidth tests record 19.82 GB/sec read and 18.77 GB/sec write. In lightweight AI evaluation, the 0.25 T4 GPU achieves 233.71 tokens per second for prompt processing and 64.28 tokens per second for generation on a small 135M parameter language model.

From an infrastructure perspective, this fractional GPU configuration offers a cost-efficient entry point for environments that require hardware graphics rendering or light acceleration without paying for a full enterprise GPU. The key operational tradeoffs are the lack of bundled local storage, constrained 2 Gbps networking, and modest CPU throughput.

The ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is well matched for virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), lightweight 3D visualization, CAD review, UI testing, and low-concurrency small-scale machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m4-vws.xlarge is a virtual workstation instance tailored for lightweight GPU-accelerated computing. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 23 GB of memory, and a fractional 0.25 partition of an NVIDIA T4 GPU equipped with 4 GB of VRAM. It operates without onboard local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate modest general-purpose compute metrics, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2011.0 and single-core score of 904.0, while small-scale LLM testing shows viable lightweight inference. By virtualizing a fraction of an enterprise GPU, this server provides a cost-effective alternative to full GPU instances for applications where full accelerator utilization is unnecessary. It is appropriately configured for cloud-hosted graphical workstations, entry-level computer-aided design, remote rendering, and entry-tier machine learning inference workloads.
